profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the model architecture lead and the systems evaluation lead for a paper-ready implementation of MEANet, a complexity-aware edge-cloud distributed AI system. They need to align on handoffs for the next internal milestone: integrating the latest edge model checkpoints with the runtime evaluator, producing the shared results table for CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, and preparing the experiment package that another lab member will use for final paper figures. The agenda is to confirm what artifact will be handed off this week, what counts as the 'integrated pipeline' being ready, which checkpoint/config should feed the evaluator, and where the shared summary sheet will live. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on interfaces, status, and ownership of the handoff artifacts, even though several subtle assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.expertise: Adaptive inference architectures, confidence calibration, multi-exit neural networks for resource-constrained devices
members.background: A postdoctoral researcher who designed the MEANet training recipe and maintains the training codebase for ResNet- and MobileNetV2-based variants across CIFAR-100 and ImageNet.
members.private_state: She wants to freeze the training side quickly so the paper narrative stays stable, and she is worried that last-minute systems requests will force retraining or expose inconsistencies between old and new checkpoints.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the model is 'integrated', they mean the evaluator can run against the latest training-produced checkpoints with the standard exported metadata, even if some runtime logging fields are still rough.
The 'current ImageNet run' refers to the latest resumed training job with temperature-scaled confidence thresholds that replaced last week's candidate checkpoint.
A 'results table' for coordination means top-line aggregate metrics per architecture-dataset pair, not per-exit or per-device breakdowns unless explicitly requested.
The shared experiment package should live in the training artifacts folder in the lab's object store, with downstream teams pulling from that canonical source.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: Edge deployment, runtime instrumentation, energy/latency benchmarking, experiment packaging for reproducible evaluation
members.background: A senior PhD student who owns the edge-cloud runtime harness, device-level measurement scripts, and the benchmarking workflow used to generate figures for internal reviews and papers.
members.private_state: He needs a stable package that his benchmarking scripts can consume without manual fixes, and he is concerned that model-side changes will break comparability across previously collected energy measurements.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the pipeline is 'integrated', they mean the checkpoint, routing metadata, thresholds, and runtime hooks all work end-to-end in the benchmarking harness without adapter code.
The 'current ImageNet run' refers to the last fully benchmarked checkpoint from Friday, because that is the only version already paired with energy traces and device logs.
A 'results table' means the reproducibility sheet used for paper figures, including per-exit routing rates, cloud-offload percentage, and device-specific energy columns.
The shared experiment package should be a versioned bundle in the evaluation repo release folder so anyone reproducing figures gets the exact config, logs, and scripts together.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the integrated pipeline being ready
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to getting the 'integrated pipeline ready' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means the newest MEANet checkpoints and routing metadata can be loaded by the evaluator and produce valid predictions on the standard validation path.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means the full edge-cloud benchmark harness runs end-to-end on device with logging, routing, and energy measurement outputs in the expected schema, requiring no manual patching.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a coordination meeting, 'ready' sounds like a shared milestone term and both expect the other to infer the obvious operational details from prior work; because both are cooperative and discussing a handoff, neither pauses to unpack the acceptance criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: Which ImageNet checkpoint is the current run
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both mention using the 'current ImageNet run' for the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the latest resumed ImageNet training run that incorporated updated confidence calibration and produced a new checkpoint over the weekend.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the Friday ImageNet checkpoint already benchmarked on the Jetson device and linked to existing energy traces.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both versions are legitimate recent candidates and are naturally referred to as 'the current run'; because each person has a different operational anchor—latest training artifact versus latest benchmarked artifact—the phrase feels specific enough without explicit naming.

misalignment_points.topic: What the results table should contain
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to update the 'results table' before the next milestone.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the table includes only consolidated top-line accuracy, average cloud-offload rate, and overall energy reduction for each backbone-dataset setting that supports the paper narrative.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the table includes those top-line numbers plus per-exit routing shares, threshold settings, device-specific latency/energy columns, and notes on benchmark conditions needed for figure generation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have repeatedly used the same phrase in prior work, but one treats it as a summary artifact while the other treats it as the master reproducibility sheet; since both are discussing 'the table' as a familiar shared object, the scope mismatch remains hidden.

misalignment_points.topic: Where the shared package will be posted
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Lina will 'drop the package in the shared folder' for Arjun to pick up.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to upload checkpoints, JSON configs, and a short README to the training team's object-store folder that already houses model artifacts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a versioned package committed or attached in the evaluation repo's release directory, including the exact wrapper scripts and manifest his harness consumes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both labs colloquially call their canonical storage location 'the shared folder,' and because the conversation centers on timing rather than the mechanics of retrieval, the procedural difference sounds too mundane to surface.
